doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Nat Adderley, Nancy Wilson and Gene Bertoncini
summary: Jenkins is a huge Nat Adderley fan, recalls asking Nancy Wilson about her album with Cannonball, and mentions Bertoncini's record with her.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Okay. Here’s one last thing. This is just a personal favorite.

Oh I love Nat Adderley. Well one person — it kind of gave it away because I knew it was Cannonball, but I’m a huge, like one of my — that’s cornet — I’m a huge Nat Adderley fan. Oh I love Nat Adderley. You know we talk about our desert island records, the record that Cannonball and Nancy Wilson did.
Oh I can’t believe you said that.

I mean Nat — Nat’s all over that thing. Nat Adderley is one of the most underrated trumpet players. He was so funky and swinging and he had great chops and a great sound. But every note was swinging. Oh man I’m a huge fan of Nat Adderley.

Oh I love that record. That’s a fantastic record. Oh. I got to ask Nancy Wilson about that one time because she was singing with the Clayton band and I had a moment, it was just a gift, I said I want to ask you about it. And she said, “yeah, people ask me about that all the time.” I said, “was that just so fun?” And she said, “oh, Zawinul and, what a band.” You know.

And the little arrangements they had behind her. I’m a big, basically both of them, Adderley nut. And I used to think when I would listen to their stuff a lot of times they would do a lot of stuff in unison. And I always thought boy if I was arranging that I would have done a harmony. Well that’s why they’re who they are. They sort of knew that. It sounded like one voice.

Yeah. And you’d go to see them and there was a high mic and a low mic. And Cannonball would play on the high mic, and Nat, who was much smaller, would play on the low mic. Right? Oh man, yeah, I’m a huge fan. You know we were talking about Gene Bertoncini who is a huge fan. He got to do a record with Nancy Wilson, it’s called “But Beautiful.” And it was Gene and Hank Jones and I think Ron Carter and Grady Tate I want to say or somebody on drums. And they did it, no solos. Hank may play eight bars

here or there. The tunes are super short. And they finished it and they were going to add strings and they listened to it and they decided not to because it’s just so great. And that was such a credit to Gene that he got to do that kind of stuff and he was such a great accompanist and such a great player.
